scientific_justification_status: Partially justified as indicator of severe disturbance, but unverified as specific partial harvest marker.
scientific_rationale_and_critique: In carp aquaculture, fish do not lose 100g of somatic weight in 14-30 days under normal farm conditions. However, in small juveniles (200g), a 100g loss is 50% body mass, whereas in large market fish (2,000g), 100g is only 5% (well within cast-net sampling variance). A flat 100g threshold across all weight stages is a coarse heuristic rather than a biologically scaled threshold.

Losing more than 5.0 grams per day over multiple weeks is biologically impossible in live fish without mass mortality, starvation catabolism, or netting of larger specimens. Pairs with ADG < -5.0 g/day (reaching up to -244 g/day) unambiguously represent commercial harvest thinning, draining, or complete cycle restocking.

scientific_justification_status: Verified as data entry or species attribution error.
scientific_rationale_and_critique: For Indian major carps (Catla catla, Labeo rohita), published aquaculture literature (FAO Fisheries Technical Papers, ICAR-CIFA manuals) establishes maximum somatic growth under intensive warm-water feeding at 2.5 to 4.5 g/day. An ADG > 20.0 g/day (e.g. 150g in 3.9 days) is biologically impossible for a single carp cohort and represents visual misclassification, species swapping, or recording errors.
Gaining 800g within a scheduled revisit interval of 3 to 45 days requires sustained daily gain of 18 to 266 g/day, far beyond physiological assimilation limits of freshwater finfish.

scientific_justification_status: Verified as appropriate for farm visit dynamics.
scientific_rationale_and_critique: Excludes sub-revisit noise (< 3 days, where true growth is zero) and prevents bridging across abandoned or completed culture cycles (> 45 days).
